The 10 KPIs Local Business Owners Need to Measure Marketing ROI (Bookmark this for later 🔖) Most local businesses struggle with this question: "Is my marketing actually working?" The answer lies in tracking the right KPIs—the ones that directly measure ROI and impact growth. Here’s the list every business owner should follow: 1. Website Traffic & Engagement 🚦 Unique Monthly Visitors – Who’s checking out your site? Segment traffic sources (organic, paid, or social) for clearer insights. Bounce Rate – Are visitors leaving quickly, not taking a desired action? High bounce rates aren’t always “bad” (there’s context) but it could mean a poor landing page experience. Average Dwell Time (Session Duration) – How long are people sticking around? More time = higher engagement. 2. Conversion Metrics 💸 Conversion Rate – Tracks the % of visitors who take action (e.g., buy something or sign up). Higher = better. Cost Per Lead (CPL) – Measures how much you’re paying for each lead. Lower CPL = more efficiency. Cost Per Acquisition (CPA) – Tracks how much it costs to acquire a paying customer. 3. Local-Specific Metrics 📍 Attributed Store Visits – Tracks how many in-store visits result directly from online campaigns. Geographic Coverage Index (GCI) – Measures local ad performance across targeted regions. 4. ROI-Focused Metrics 📊 Return on Ad Spend (ROAS) – Calculates how much revenue you’re earning for every ad dollar spent. Formula: ROAS = (Revenue ÷ Ad Spend) x 100 Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) – Predicts the total revenue a customer will generate over their relationship with you. 5. Calculating ROI (the BIG one) Formula: (Revenue - Cost) ÷ Cost x 100 Example: Spent $1,000 on ads. Made $5,000 in revenue. Your ROI? 400%. 💥 6. Use Tools for Tracking 🛠 Google Analytics, Google Search Console, HubSpot, and SEMrush can be your best friends for monitoring these metrics. Pro Tip: Focus on data-driven decisions, not guesswork. Track these KPIs consistently. Double down on what’s working. Fix what’s not. Which KPI do you prioritize in your business? Comment below! ⬇️

# ROI Tracking: A Comprehensive Guide for Marketers

[Telmo Silva](https://www.clicdata.com/blog/author/telmosilva/)on October 25, 2023

Last updated on August 7, 2025

One of the most important aspects of building a successful marketing campaign is finding out if you’re getting a suitable return. That’s where the power of measuring your return on investment (ROI) comes into play. 

Since your ad campaigns don’t run on infinite financial resources, it’s up to you to make sure costs are commensurate with results. 

Otherwise, you could end up overspending on a campaign that doesn’t do any justice for your brand or lead generation. Still, mastering ROI tracking can be challenging as a marketer.

In this guide, we’ll explain how you can better track marketing ROI for your paid advertising campaigns so you can make informed decisions.

**TL;DR**

*   **Determine your “Whys”** in order to measure the right metrics and have a clear understanding of your campaign ROI,
*   **Make the distinction between goals and priorities**, the goal being your destination and the priorities being the route to get you there more rapidly,
*   **Establish the right KPIs**, are you expecting an increase in traffic increase, clicks, or revenue,
*   **Target niche markets** to make your messaging heard and remembered by your target audience while lowering your CPL,
*   **Segment your activities** to make your data more manageable and derive actionable insights from it,
*   **Monitor your traffic sources** and measure the impact of your paid search ads on your marketing goals,
*   **Perform competitor research** and identify new behaviour and patterns in your ICP buying journey,
*   **Schedule regular team meetings** to review your campaign metrics and brainstorm to optimize your budget,
*   **Integrate and automate** your data analysis process with a data analytics platform to make decisions based on reliable and up-to-date data,
*   **Document your strategy** to keep track of all your internal strategic meetings and build a solid knowledge base for you and your team,
*   **Ask your customers** why they chose your products or services to refine your messaging and invest in the right channels – and increase your ROI!

Alright, now the long story:

## Determine Your “Whys”

The first step in marketing ROI tracking is figuring out why you’re creating a marketing campaign in the first place. 

Are you creating paid ads to drive more traffic to your website? Do you want to increase the exposure of your products, services, or content? Or do you want to maximize your website’s conversion rate?

Marketing ROI tracking looks different for every business running a paid advertising campaign. Once you identify your “whys,” you can determine which metrics matter most. 

That way, the data you collect in Google Analytics from Google Ads or Facebook Ads are that much more meaningful.

## Make the Distinction Between Goals and Priorities

Goals and priorities, though often used interchangeably, serve distinct functions in your marketing strategy. 

Goals are the specific, measurable outcomes you aim for over a set period. They act as a compass directing your path. For example, maybe your goal is to increase website traffic in the UK by 15% in Q4. 

Meanwhile, priorities determine the sequence of your actions. When you answer the common question, “What should I work on next?” That’s prioritization. 

[](https://colinscotland.com/what-is-the-most-important-step-in-prioritizing-goals/)

source: [Colin Scotland](https://colinscotland.com/what-is-the-most-important-step-in-prioritizing-goals/)

Unlike goals, priorities can shift based on circumstances — making them dynamic and adaptable. However, the relationship between the two is symbiotic. 

While goals map your destination, priorities help you navigate the best route. What’s the key to ‌higher marketing ROI over the shortest period? Adjusting priorities based on external factors and emerging challenges.

For instance, one might prioritize optimizing ad copy over competitor research based on immediate needs or potential impact. 

Don’t skip this step. With clear, defined goals and regular assessment of your priorities, you establish a focused and effective journey toward business success.
